subject: ss-neurosurgery
title: Brain metastases and SRS: cavity control, Gamma Knife, WBRT and spine scores

steps.say: Metastases are the commonest brain tumours and they are arising from lung, breast, melanoma, kidney and bowel primaries. Small round grey-white junction lesions with oedema are suggesting mets over glioma. Multiplicity is favouring spread over primary.
steps.tx: Metastases are the commonest brain tumours, arising from a lung primary and from breast, melanoma, renal and colorectal primaries, and multiple small round **grey-white junction** lesions with oedema suggest mets over glioma. A solitary lesion in a cancer patient still needs tissue proof. Unknown primary triggers chest and body imaging.

steps.say: A large symptomatic lesion is removed first when diagnosis is uncertain or pressure is high. The cavity is then treated with focused radiosurgery. Cognition is preserved far better than with whole-brain treatment.
steps.tx: A large symptomatic or diagnostic-uncertain lesion is resected followed by **cavity radiosurgery** (stereotactic), which controls the bed with less cognitive injury than whole-brain radiotherapy. Surgery also gives tissue when the primary is unknown. Cavity SRS starts once the wound heals.

steps.say: Gamma Knife is treating up to four small lesions in one session with single-fraction doses. Larger volumes are handled with staged or fractionated schedules. A four-centimetre ceiling is guiding the choice.
steps.tx: **Gamma Knife** radiosurgery with 12 to 24 Gy single-fraction marginal dose treats up to 4 lesions below 3 to 4 cm, and staged or fractionated SRS extends control to larger volumes. Dose falls with size to protect normal brain. New lesions later get repeat SRS.

rows: Up to 4 lesions below 3 to 4 cm

steps.say: Whole-brain treatment is reserved for miliary disease and leptomeningeal spread. Hippocampal avoidance with memantine is limiting memory loss. Focal options are preferred whenever counts allow.
steps.tx: Whole-brain radiotherapy is reserved for miliary disease and leptomeningeal spread, using **hippocampal avoidance** with memantine to limit memory loss. Sparing the hippocampi preserves recall. Memantine continues for months after radiation ends. Baseline cognition is recorded before starting. Hippocampal sparing suits patients with good prognosis.

vis.alt: Diagram of neuraxis tumour seeding with sugar-coating MRI, cauda equina enhancement and lumbar puncture showing malignant CSF cells.
vis.caption: Neuraxis seeding with sugar-coating MRI and malignant CSF cytology marks leptomeningeal spread. Credit: StewardMD.

steps.say: Small-cell lung cancer with good response is receiving prophylactic cranial irradiation. Driver-mutated lung and HER2 breast disease are getting brain-penetrant drugs. Local and systemic control are planned together.
steps.tx: Small-cell lung cancer with good response gets **prophylactic cranial irradiation**, while NSCLC with driver mutation and HER2 breast disease get CNS-penetrant therapy (systemic) alongside local control. Irradiation halves brain relapse after response. Penetrant drugs treat microscopic deposits everywhere. Response is confirmed on imaging before booking.

steps.say: Prognosis is graded from age, performance, extracranial control and lesion count. Good-score patients are offered aggressive local therapy. Poor scores are steering toward supportive care.
steps.tx: Graded **prognostic assessment** combines age, performance status, extracranial control and lesion count to select aggressive local therapy versus supportive care. The score is recalculated when disease changes. Honest grading avoids futile craniotomy. Frail patients with progressing systemic disease are guided toward comfort.

steps.say: Spinal secondaries are scored for instability and cord compression separately. High-grade compression with instability is needing separation surgery plus focused radiation. Radiation alone is failing where bone is collapsing.
steps.tx: Spinal metastases are graded by the **SINS score** for instability and the Bilsky grade for cord compression (ESCC scale), and high-grade compression with instability gets separation surgery plus spine SBRT rather than radiotherapy alone. Separation creates a millimetre gap for safe dosing. Stable low-grade compression may take radiation alone.

vis.alt: Vertebral metastasis compressing the cord with sagittal MRI, red-flag symptoms and emergency management steps.
vis.caption: Vertebral metastasis with cord compression, red flags and emergency steps. Credit: StewardMD.

steps.say: Survival is estimated from primary type, visceral spread, neurology and performance. Long survivors are offered en bloc excision with curative intent. Short survivors are receiving palliation or radiation.
steps.tx: The **Tokuhashi score** and Tomita score estimate survival from primary type, visceral mets and neurology to choose en bloc excision, palliation or radiotherapy for spinal secondaries. High predicted survival justifies major excision. Low scores favour short-course radiation and comfort. Scores are repeated when staging changes.
